humanTitle: People who cancelled a trial were billed for the year anyway
whoItAffects: iPhone and Android users in Australia, the United States and Canada, across two app versions.

build.proposition: A trial that names the charge date and the amount before it starts, and again before it lands.
specifics: Send the reminder from the app, not only from the store
Show the cancellation state the store holds, so the two cannot disagree
Confirm a cancellation in writing at the moment it is made
build.limitation: The billing relationship belongs to the app store, and the app cannot always see or change what it did.

start.proposition: A subscription record kept outside whoever is selling the subscription.
specifics: Reads the store receipt rather than the seller’s own dashboard
Warns before any trial converts, across everything at once
start.limitation: Receipt access is granted by the store and can be withdrawn, and trials converting quietly is what the stores earn from.

study.proposition: How many people who believe they cancelled were still charged?
specifics: Compare the store’s cancellation record with what people report doing
Separate a mistimed cancellation from one that never registered
study.limitation: Only the store holds the ground truth on either side, and it does not publish it.

write.proposition: The week between cancelling and being charged for the year.
specifics: Follow one refusal through the app, the store and the card
Quote the reviewer who cancelled two days early and paid anyway
write.limitation: Every subscription story reads the same way until the receipts are actually in it.
